headline: Getting Plumbing Rough-In Right the First Time
articleBody: Getting the plumbing rough-in right is absolutely crucial for any kitchen or bath remodel, especially here in Berkeley and the wider East Bay. It's essentially the backbone of your water system, tucked away behind your walls. The rough-in phase typically involves installing all the water supply lines, drainpipes, and vent pipes that will eventually connect to your fixtures. This work absolutely has to happen before walls can be closed up and before any insulation is installed. A key step is confirming the rough-in route with your contractor, ensuring it aligns with your design plans and local codes. You also need to coordinate access with other trades, like framing, HVAC, and electrical, so everyone has the space they need without creating clashes. Most importantly, a plumbing inspection is required before anything gets covered up. You'll want to verify that all necessary materials and fixtures are on site *before* the plumbing crew mobilizes to avoid delays. Mistakes here mean opening up finished walls later, which is a costly and messy fix. A licensed plumber or experienced construction coordinator is essential to ensure code compliance and prevent future headaches.
